{
  "screen_decision": "exclude",
  "screen_rationale": "The study evaluates in silico tools (Derek Nexus and QSAR Toolbox) for predicting phototoxicity. The screening rule explicitly excludes studies where the predictor of human outcome is only a non-animal method, such as in silico/computational methods. While the abstract mentions traditional in vivo models (mice, rats, guinea pigs) and in vitro assays, these are presented as background and not as part of the study's predictive methodology or evaluation.",
  "arm": "toxicology",
  "arm_evidence": "Phototoxicity testing is crucial for evaluating the potential harmful effects of pharmaceuticals and chemicals on human skin when exposed to sunlight.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "dermatology",
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "Phototoxicity testing is crucial for evaluating the potential harmful effects of pharmaceuticals and chemicals on human skin when exposed to sunlight.",
  "model_type": "regulatory-dataset",
  "model_evidence": "The study evaluated two in silico tools - Derek Nexus 6.1.0/Derek Knowledge Base 2020 1.0 (Lhasa Limited, UK) and the QSAR Toolbox (v 4.5) developed by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) - for their capacity to predict the phototoxicity of several substances from diverse classes.",
  "species": [
    "mouse",
    "rat",
    "guinea-pig"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "Traditional in vivo models involving mice, rats, guinea pigs, as well as in vitro assays such as the 3T3 Neutral Red Uptake phototoxicity assay and methods based on the use of reconstructed human epidermis, have been established for phototoxicity testing.",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "Derek Nexus predicted phototoxicity of the compounds, with a sensitivity of 63%, specificity of 93%, Positive Predictive Values of 90% and Negative Predictive Value of 69%, overall accuracy of 77% and balanced accuracy of 78%."
}
